title: Microsoft Purview: sensitivity label inheritance for Teams meeting artifacts (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: Hold: the artifact control's Learn link documents policy creation but not the artifact setting itself. The download restriction is verified for recordings and transcripts, but the broader wording about encrypted artifacts also encompasses Loop notes without supporting documentation.

claims.claim: This is a Microsoft Purview information protection change.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Purview"]

claims.claim: Microsoft plans configurable inheritance of a Teams meeting's sensitivity label by recordings, transcripts and Loop notes.
claims.quote: Teams meeting artifacts, including recordings, transcripts, and Loop notes, can now be configured to automatically inherit the sensitivity label from the meeting.

claims.claim: The planned inheritance reduces the need for manual labeling.
claims.quote: This ensures content generated during meetings is consistently protected without requiring manual labeling, reducing risk and simplifying protection at scale.

claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: Apply meeting label to artifacts is a documented sensitivity label publishing policy setting.
claims.quote: Configure label policy settings that are specific just to calendar items, Teams meetings, and chat: ... Apply meeting label to artifacts

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The setting automatically applies the meeting's sensitivity label to recordings.
claims.quote: For Teams meetings, automatically apply the meeting's sensitivity label to recordings and their transcripts (.mp4 files)

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The setting also applies the label to the recordings' transcripts.
claims.quote: For Teams meetings, automatically apply the meeting's sensitivity label to recordings and their transcripts (.mp4 files)

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The setting also applies the label to meeting notes in .loop files.
claims.quote: and to meeting notes (.loop files) at the time the artifact is saved to SharePoint or OneDrive.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Scope
claims.claim: Inheritance happens when the artifact is saved to SharePoint or OneDrive.
claims.quote: at the time the artifact is saved to SharePoint or OneDrive.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: An inherited label does not automatically change after a subsequent meeting label change.
claims.quote: If the meeting label changes later, the inherited label doesn't automatically change.

claims.claim: Learn marks the artifact setting as preview.
claims.quote: This setting is in preview and for MP4 files, requires you to enable sensitivity labeling support for MP4.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: MP4 sensitivity labeling support must be enabled for the setting to label MP4 recordings.
claims.quote: If MP4 support isn't enabled, these files aren't labeled when you select this option.

claims.claim: Learn does not state the artifact setting's availability in GCC, GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" "GCC"; "Apply meeting label to artifacts" licensing default GCC. Read sensitivity-labels-meetings and government deployment search excerpts; none states this setting's government-cloud availability.

claims.claim: Encrypting labels for MP4 files must use Assign permissions now rather than user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels that apply encryption must be configured with the Assign permissions now option, rather than user-defined permissions.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the artifact setting's default on arrival, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" "default"; "Apply meeting label to artifacts" licensing default GCC. Read roadmap description and sensitivity-labels-meetings; neither states whether artifact inheritance starts enabled.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: impact
claims.claim: A sensitivity label applying encryption prevents downloading the recording and transcript.
claims.quote: However, if a recording and transcript has a label that applies encryption, you can't download them.

claims.claim: Recordings respect the label encryption's access permissions and usage rights.
claims.quote: Recordings respect any access permissions and usage rights from label encryption settings

claims.claim: A label without encryption permits downloading the recording and transcript.
claims.quote: You can download them if the label doesn't apply encryption

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: impact
claims.claim: A downloaded recording or transcript with an unencrypted label loses the labeling information.
claims.quote: but a downloaded file in this case doesn't retain the labeling information.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Encrypted labeled recordings can play in a browser despite the download restriction.
claims.quote: can be played directly in a web browser and supported experiences such as SharePoint, Teams, or Clipchamp.

claims.claim: These files can be manually relabeled using their Details pane in SharePoint or OneDrive.
claims.quote: You can, if required, manually relabel these files in SharePoint or OneDrive, by using the file's Details pane.

claims.claim: Relabeling encrypted content requires appropriate permissions, which the meeting owner has.
claims.quote: As with all sensitivity labels, you must have the appropriate permissions to change a sensitivity label that applies encryption, which is always the case for the meeting owner.

claims.claim: No approval step is documented for artifact inheritance.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" "approval". Read sensitivity-labels-meetings: it describes automatic application at save time and no approval step; search returned no relevant approval procedure.

claims.claim: The meetings labeling page publishes no price or meter for this setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting artifact inheritance sensitivity labels licensing price meter; "Apply meeting label to artifacts" approval role price. Read sensitivity-labels-meetings and the Purview service description; no setting-specific price or meter found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Purview service description says sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires Microsoft 365 E5 or IPG.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy‑based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.claim: The service description lists manual sensitivity labeling for Teams online meetings under Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 plus Teams Premium.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 + Teams Premium ... Manual Sensitivity Labeling for Teams online meetings | Included | Included

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Some options on the meetings labeling page cannot be configured without Teams Premium in the tenant.
claims.quote: You won't be able to configure all the options referenced on this page if a Teams Premium license isn't found for your tenant.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No license statement specific to the artifact inheritance setting is published beyond the general labeling and meeting requirements.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting artifact inheritance sensitivity labels licensing price meter; "Apply meeting label to artifacts" licensing default GCC. Read sensitivity-labels-meetings and the Purview service description; neither singles out this setting's entitlement.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects general Purview labeling entitlements and additional Teams Premium requirements for some meeting options.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 + Teams Premium

claims.claim: Protecting meetings requires the Files & other data assets, Emails and Meetings label scopes.
claims.quote: Files & other data assets; Emails; Meetings. All three options are needed because of their interdependency.

claims.claim: The meeting label must be published to meeting organizers and participants.
claims.quote: Make sure the label is published to meeting organizers and participants.

claims.claim: Label meeting options cannot be enforced for users whose Teams clients do not meet the documented requirements.
claims.quote: If meeting participants or organizers don't use a Teams client that meets these requirements, the configured label meeting options can't be enforced for these users.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The linked create-sensitivity-labels page documents the route through Publishing policies and Publish label to Apply meeting label to artifacts.
claims.quote: On the Label policies page, select Publish label to start the Create policy configuration.
claims.fix: Keep the path, which is supported across the two cited pages, but change controls[0].ui.docs and the corresponding rendered table link to https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels-meetings#configure-a-corresponding-sensitivity-label-publishing-policy. That page documents Apply meeting label to artifacts; create-sensitivity-labels documents only the route into policy configuration.

claims.claim: No operation or advanced-setting key for scripting artifact inheritance is documented in the searched references.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" PowerShell Set-LabelPolicy. Read Set-LabelPolicy, its AdvancedSettings list, create-sensitivity-labels and sensitivity-labels-meetings; no artifact-inheritance operation or deciding key found.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles $true enables sensitivity labeling support for MP4 files.
claims.quote: To turn on support for MP4 video files, use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles parameter: Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles $true

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: No admin UI control for enabling MP4 sensitivity label support is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles" admin center enable. Read sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files and video-purview search excerpts; they prescribe SharePoint Online PowerShell, not a UI setting for MP4 support.

claims.claim: The MP4 support setting also controls Clipchamp project labeling.
claims.quote: The same setting also controls sensitivity label behavior for Clipchamp projects.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises allowing 24 hours for label and policy changes before troubleshooting.
claims.quote: For labels and label policy settings, allow 24 hours for the changes to propagate through the services.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Label policy settings apply to the selected users and groups, permitting a pilot audience.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy documents an advanced setting for mandatory meeting labels.
claims.quote: TeamworkMandatory: Outlook and Teams apps that support this setting can enable or disable mandatory labeling for meetings.

claims.claim: The SharePoint MP4 setting has tenant scope, qualified by the connected geo-location in Multi-Geo.
claims.quote: The setting applies across the tenant, or the connected geo-location in a Multi-Geo organization; review its effect before changing it.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Multi-Geo tenants must connect to each geo-location and run the MP4 command separately.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo, you must connect to each of your geo-locations and run the command separately.

claims.claim: Learn's description of the artifact setting does not itself name a configuring administrator role.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" approval role price. Read the full artifact-setting description in sensitivity-labels-meetings; it specifies relabeling permissions but names no administrator role for configuring the policy setting.

claims.claim: Encrypted artifacts, including the Loop notes named in this bullet, cannot be downloaded.
claims.quote: Searched: Loop files sensitivity labels encryption download restrictions .loop. Read sensitivity-labels-meetings, sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files and sensitivity-labels-loop; the download prohibition is stated for recordings/transcripts and MP4, not Loop notes.
claims.fix: Replace 'since encrypted artifacts can't be downloaded' with 'since recordings and transcripts with labels that apply encryption cannot be downloaded', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels-meetings#configure-a-corresponding-sensitivity-label-publishing-policy.

claims.claim: An existing label policy can be edited by selecting it and using Edit Policy.
claims.quote: To edit an existing label policy, select it, and then select the Edit Policy button from the flyout pane:

claims.claim: An unlabeled meeting has no meeting sensitivity label for its artifacts to inherit.
claims.quote: For Teams meetings, automatically apply the meeting's sensitivity label to recordings and their transcripts (.mp4 files), and to meeting notes (.loop files)

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy documents an advanced setting for default meeting labels.
claims.quote: teamworkdefaultlabelid: Outlook and Teams apps that support this setting apply a default label, or no label for meetings.
